context: Saturday morning. Daichi calls Kenji from Osaka to figure out plans for the evening.
purpose: friend logistics with banter — casual Kansai-Tokyo phone call between close mates

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.en: Oi — where are you right now?
lines.style: Loud, energetic opener. Stretch the 「おーい」 playfully with Kansai enthusiasm. No preamble—straight into the ask. Full volume, full presence.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: 今うちだよ。なに、もう外おる？
lines.en: I'm at home. What—you out already?
lines.style: Half-laugh threaded through. Pick up a single Kansai inflection ironically, showing you're used to this. Warm, loose, in-the-middle-of-something-but-glad-he-called.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.jp: まだまだ。今日さ、本当に時間ある？
lines.en: Not yet. Listen—do you actually have time today?
lines.style: Drop half a register into mock-serious. The 「本当に」 is a real question underneath the performance—fishing to check commitment before making the plan.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.style: Calm, ready, purposefully low-energy. Not matching Daichi's volume—letting him drive. Clear and direct, no performance.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.jp: 七時に駅でどう？飲み行こ。
lines.en: Seven at the station—how's that? Let's go drink.
lines.style: Lift and lean on 「どう？」 expectantly, then flatten and solidify on 「飲み行こ」. Plan-making mode shifting to decided. Kansai throughout.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: 七時了解。一緒に行く店、もう決めた？
lines.en: Seven, got it. You picked the place yet?
lines.style: Brisk acknowledgment, then a small teasing prod underneath. Knows he hasn't. The question lands light, affectionate—not an accusation.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.jp: (笑) おまえなぁ、それは今から決めるねん！
lines.en: (laughs) Oi, that's what we're deciding now!
lines.style: Big, real laugh leading. Volume rises back up. Full Kansai on the 「ねん」 ending. Mock-outrage—he's been called out and he knows it. Performed loud and proud.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: はいはい、じゃあ明日には決まってるってことで。
lines.en: Yeah, yeah—so let's say it'll be decided by tomorrow then.
lines.style: Dry, tired-friend callback. The 「はいはい」 lands as gentle exhaustion—affectionate underneath. Small smile underneath it all. Not unkind, just honest.
